parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
When chlorine dissolves in water the following reaction occurs.

$$\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{HClO(aq)} + \text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Cl}^-\text{(aq)}$$

When solutions of chlorine are used for water purification, the pH of the solution of chlorine is kept near to pH 7 by the addition of a base.

Chlorine is dissolved in water to produce $1000\text{ cm}^3$ of a solution containing $0.170\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HClO}$ and $0.170\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$.

A buffer solution is then prepared by adding $0.200\text{ mol}$ of $\text{NaOH(s)}$ to this solution. The $\text{NaOH}$ reacts initially with the $\text{HCl}$.

Calculate the pH of the buffer solution.

[$\text{HClO}$ is a weak acid with $K_\text{a} = 2.9 \times 10^{-8}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.]
